text:
jenna: hey team :wave: first day here. trying to build the inference runtime from source and hitting a linker/runtime error. anyone available to point me to the right setup?

sam: welcome! :tada: what OS and GPU drivers are you on? paste outputs of `uname -a`, `nvidia-smi`, and `nvcc --version` if you can.

jenna: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
jenna: here's `nvidia-smi` output:
```
Tue Mar 23 10:12:33 2026
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 515.48.07    Driver Version: 515.48.07    CUDA Version: 11.7     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| 0    A10          Off               00000000:01:00.0  On   |                   0 |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

jenna: and `nvcc --version` shows:
```
nvcc: NVIDIA (R) Cuda compiler driver
Built on Mon_Jun_6_2025
Cuda compilation tools, release 12.1, V12.1.105
```

jenna: build error snippet: 
```
/opt/redwood/runtime/lib/libcuda.so: undefined reference to `cuGetProcAddress'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
CMakeFiles/runtime.dir/build.make:123: recipe for target runtime failed
```

mike: hmm looks like driver/runtime mismatch — driver is 515.x but nvcc/toolkit is 12.1. That causes missing symbols. Are you compiling with CUDA 12 flags? Our default CI image is built against CUDA 11.8 currently.

jenna: I did set `-DCUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR=/usr/local/cuda-12.1` in the cmake invocation. also saw a ptxas error earlier: `ptxas fatal : Value 'sm_86' is not recognized`

ryan: ptxas error usually means nvcc and GPU arch flags don't align with the toolkit or driver. Which GPU is that exactly? A10 should be sm_80 or sm_86 depending on revision. Try setting `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=86` or exporting `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=8.6`.

mike: alternatively if you want to avoid driver changes for now, you can build a CPU-only variant to continue with tests: `bazel build //runtime:core --define=enable_cuda=false` — that will unblock local dev.

jenna: tried `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=86` but linker still failing. Is there a recommended driver version in the onboarding doc?

sam: we keep a short matrix in the eng-runtime onboarding doc. tl;dr: CUDA toolkit 12.x -> driver >= 525.x, CUDA toolkit 11.8 -> driver >= 515.x. If your nvcc says 12.1 you need to upgrade the driver. I'll paste the doc link: https://redwood.internal/eng-runtime/onboarding#cuda

build-bot: CI job #4321 on master reported similar linker failure earlier — full log: https://ci.redwood/builds/4321/logs

jenna: ok i'll try upgrading driver. quick question: should i symlink `/usr/local/cuda` to the toolkit dir or rely on `CUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR` in cmake?

ryan: symlink is fine for local dev and many tools expect `/usr/local/cuda`. For reproducible builds we prefer explicit `CUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR`. Either works but make sure `nvcc` in PATH matches that dir: `which nvcc` and `nvcc --version`.

jenna: update — installed driver 535.86 and symlinked `/usr/local/cuda -> /usr/local/cuda-12.1`. re-ran cmake with `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=86`. Build succeeded! :tada:

sam: :thumbsup: awesome — can you add a short note to the eng-runtime README about driver/toolkit pairs (so future new hires don't hit this)?

jenna: will do, i'll add a one-paragraph note and attach the `nvidia-smi`/`nvcc` pair I used.

mike: welcome aboard again, and great debugging. ping if you want a quick walkthrough of the CI image and devcontainer later.

jenna: thanks everyone — appreciate the help!
